# L3 VSN, VRF and Routing

_Extreme Fabric Engine · 29 commands_

VRFs and L3 VSNs (IP VPN over SPB), IP interfaces, routes, ARP, inter-VRF leaking, VRRP/RSMLT, DHCP relay, OSPF/BGP basics and Segmented VRF.

## Details

### `show ip route [<ip> | -s <prefix/len>] [vrf <vrf>]`

```
show ip route vrf CORP
show ip route 10.20.30.40 vrf CORP
show ip route -s 10.20.0.0/16 vrf CORP
```

The PROT column shows ISIS for routes from other BEBs (L3 VSN or IP shortcuts), LOC for local and STAT for static routes. The next hop of an IS-IS route is the hostname of the remote BEB.


### `show isis spbm ip-unicast-fib [all] [id <isid>]`

```
show isis spbm ip-unicast-fib all
show isis spbm ip-unicast-fib id 30001
```

If a prefix is missing in `show ip route vrf X`, check here whether any BEB announces it at all.


### `show ip arp [vlan <vid> | vrf <vrf> | <ip>]`

```
show ip arp 10.10.100.25
show ip arp vrf CORP
```

`show ip arp spbm-tunnel-as-mac` shows entries learned across the fabric with the remote B-MAC.


### `show ip interface [vrf <vrf>]`

Only primary addresses. `show ip address [secondary] [vrf <vrf>]` lists all, including secondary ones.


### `show ip ipvpn [vrf <vrf>]`

For a Segmented VRF (9.4+), the output also shows the trusted, unrestricted and untrusted I-SIDs.


### `ip vrf <vrf> vrfid <1-511>`

```
ip vrf CORP vrfid 10
```

The VRF ID is only locally significant. Across the fabric only the L3 VSN I-SID counts. Using the same name and ID everywhere still makes life easier.


### `router vrf <vrf>`

```
router vrf CORP
  ipvpn
  i-sid 30010
  ipvpn enable
  isis redistribute direct
  isis redistribute direct enable
  exit
isis apply redistribute direct vrf CORP
```

This is the complete L3 VSN setup. The I-SID must be the same on every BEB of this VRF. Without redistribution, the VRF's subnets are not advertised into the fabric.


### `ipvpn / i-sid <isid> / ipvpn enable`

Keep L3 VSN I-SIDs in a separate number range from L2 VSN I-SIDs, e.g. 3xxxx, so they are easy to recognize.


### `isis redistribute direct [route-map <map>] [enable]`

Takes effect only after `isis apply redistribute direct vrf <vrf>`. Secondary subnets are always redistributed unless a route-map filters them.


### `isis apply redistribute <protocol> vrf <vrf>`

```
isis apply redistribute direct vrf CORP
isis apply redistribute static vrf CORP
```

Check the result with `show ip isis redistribute vrf <vrf>`.


### `isis accept i-sid <isid> enable`

```
router vrf GUEST
  isis accept i-sid 30099 enable
  exit
isis apply accept vrf GUEST
```

Use it for shared services (DNS, DHCP, firewall in its own VRF). With `ip isid-list <name> list <isids>` you can import several L3 VSNs at once (`isis accept isid-list <name> enable`), and a route-map filters which prefixes come in. Remember the reverse direction for return traffic.

> ▲ **Caution:** `isis apply accept` re-installs all IS-IS routes of the VRF. Expect a short traffic interruption.


### `interface vlan <vid>`

```
interface vlan 100
  vrf CORP
  ip address 10.10.100.1/24
  ip dhcp-relay fwd-path 10.0.0.10
  exit
```

Assign the VRF first, then the IP address.


### `vrf <vrf> [trusted | unrestricted | untrusted]`

The segment keywords exist only from 9.4 (Segmented VRF). Without a keyword, the VLAN joins the trusted segment.


### `ip address <ip/len> [secondary] [dvr-one-ip]`

```
ip address 10.10.100.1/24
```

`dvr-one-ip` marks the gateway address shared by all DvR controllers of the subnet.


### `ip route <prefix/len> <next-hop | discard> weight <1-65535> [enable]`

```
ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.255.0.1 weight 10
router vrf CORP
  ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.255.10.1 weight 10
```

Advertise static routes into the fabric with `isis redistribute static`, then `isis apply redistribute static vrf <vrf>`. `next-hop-vrf <vrf>` points a static route into another VRF. Check with `show ip route static [vrf <vrf>]`.


### `ip ecmp / ip ecmp max-path <1-8>`

Check with `show ip ecmp max-path [vrf <vrf>]`. Disabling ECMP removes all ECMP routes.


### `ip dhcp-relay fwd-path <server-ip>`

```
interface vlan 100
  ip dhcp-relay
  ip dhcp-relay fwd-path 10.0.0.10
  ip dhcp-relay fwd-path 10.0.0.11
```

`ip dhcp-relay` enables relay on the interface. If a path shows as disabled, enable it with `ip dhcp-relay fwd-path <server-ip> enable`. With VRRP, bind the path to the virtual router with `ip dhcp-relay fwd-path <server-ip> vrid <vrid>`. Check the paths with `show ip dhcp-relay fwd-path vrf <vrf>`.


### `show ip dhcp-relay counters [vrf <vrf>]`

If requests increase but replies stay at 0, check the server reachability and the return route from the server to the relay address.


### `show ip vrrp [vrf <vrf>]`

In SMLT designs, `ip vrrp <vrid> backup-master enable` makes both peers forward. On fabric designs, prefer DvR or Anycast Gateway.


### `ip vrrp address <vrid> <vip> / ip vrrp <vrid> enable`

```
interface vlan 100
  ip vrrp address 100 10.10.100.1
  ip vrrp 100 priority 200
  ip vrrp 100 backup-master enable
  ip vrrp 100 enable
```

backup-master (both SMLT peers forward for the virtual IP) is only supported on SMLT ports and must not be combined with critical IP.


### `ip rsmlt [holdup-timer <0-9999>]`

The holddown timer defaults to 60 s; set it longer than your routing convergence. A holdup timer of 9999 means "forever", which is common in L3 edge designs.


### `show ip ospf neighbor [vrf <vrf>]`

`show ip ospf interface [vrf <vrf>]` shows the interface settings (area, timers, network type) when a neighbor does not come up.


### `show ip bgp summary [vrf <vrf>]`

`show ip bgp neighbors <ip> advertised-routes|routes [vrf <vrf>]` shows what is sent and received.


### `segmented`

Clients in an untrusted VLAN only reach the unrestricted segment (for example the firewall), trusted clients reach trusted and unrestricted. IP VPN must be disabled when you enable it; re-enable IP VPN afterwards. The new segments get the suffixes -unr and -unt. Existing interfaces become trusted. With an L3 VSN it requires a Premier or subscription license. Not supported on the 7830 or on models that support only one VRF.
